title: Common-stage finite realization and natural iterated Weil structures
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its fixed algebraic closure $k$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $Y_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Write $g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ for geometric Frobenius. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the rationalized constructible categories and derived pullbacks in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Let $\mathcal C_Y=D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$ be the literal category of pairs $(E,K)$ and common-stage morphism classes of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. All composition and scalar comparisons are the specified rationalizations of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], including equality of scheme morphisms, units and finite iterations. 
Put $T_E=Lg_{Y,E}^*$ and let $T$ be its common-stage pullback. Use Weil pairs $(K,\theta:T K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ and their morphisms from [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Every finite collection of these pairs and Weil morphisms, together with finitely many equations between composites, has simultaneous finite-stage representatives over some $E$: the structure maps, their inverses, the specified arrows and all the equations are represented over $E$ and hold there. Prescribed finite starting coefficient fields may all be contained in $E$.

For $r\geq1$ define the iterated isomorphisms by $\theta_E^{[1]}=\theta_E$ and
$$\theta_E^{[r+1]}=\theta_E^{[r]}T_E^r(\theta_E):T_E^{r+1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,$$
using the specified pullback-composition comparisons to identify $T_E^r$ with $L(g_Y^r)_E^*$. For $E\subset M$, write $K_M=K\otimes_E M$ and $d_{r,K}:(T_E^rK)\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}T_M^rK_M$ for the iterated scalar comparison; give $K_M$ the structure $\theta_M=(\theta_E\otimes_E M)d_{1,K}^{-1}$. Then
$$\theta_M^{[r]}d_{r,K}=\theta_E^{[r]}\otimes_E M.$$
These isomorphisms respect the identity and tower scalar identifications and define the iterated structure $\theta^{[r]}:T^rK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ in $\mathcal C_Y$, independently of the representatives of $\theta$, its inverse, and their equations. For every Weil morphism $u:(K,\theta_K)\to(L,\theta_L)$, including noninvertible $u$,
$$u\theta_K^{[r]}=\theta_L^{[r]}T^r(u)\quad(r\geq1).$$

proof.text: Write every specified underlying object as $(E_i,K_i)$. In the literal pair category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], choose representatives of the finitely many structure maps $\theta_i$, inverse maps $\psi_i=\theta_i^{-1}$, and specified arrows. Take a common finite overfield $B$ containing all their fields and all prescribed starting fields, using the compositum upper bounds in that definition. By the description of morphisms and composition in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] (each class is represented over a common finite extension, composites are formed over a common finite extension, and the directed colimit's transition maps are scalar extension composed with the scalar identifications), induction on the finitely many arrows and composites of this finite diagram transports all of it to $B$. The vertices become $K_{i,B}=K_i\otimes_{E_i}B$, and the representatives of $T K_i$ become $(T_{E_i}K_i)\otimes_{E_i}B$. Repeated occurrences use the same vertex. At this point the representatives of the structure maps need not yet be invertible over $B$.

proof.text: Use the natural comparison $d_{1,K_i}:(T_{E_i}K_i)\otimes_{E_i}B\cong T_BK_{i,B}$ of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. If $t_i$ and $v_i$ represent $\theta_i$ and $\psi_i$, put $\theta_{i,B}=t_i d_{1,K_i}^{-1}$ and $\psi_{i,B}=d_{1,K_i}v_i$. For each specified arrow use its representative $u_B$. The finite list of equations now consists of $\theta_{i,B}\psi_{i,B}=1$, $\psi_{i,B}\theta_{i,B}=1$, every $u_B\theta_{i,B}=\theta_{j,B}T_B(u_B)$, and the prescribed equations between composites. Their classes are true by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] and the hypotheses: the action of $T$ on a representative is precisely stage pullback conjugated by the scalar comparisons. Since two representatives in the directed colimit of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] define the same class exactly when they agree after extension to a further common finite extension, every one has a finite equality witness. Enlarge $B$ to one finite field $E$ containing all these witnesses. Functorial scalar transport preserves equalities and compositions; the scalar tower equations identify the transported comparisons with the direct ones. Thus the displayed representatives over $E$ satisfy all equations, and $\psi_{i,E}$ is an actual two-sided inverse. This proves simultaneous realization without assuming transition maps on Hom sets are injective.

proof.text:
The same transport preserves Weil morphisms. Write $S=(-)\otimes_E M$ and abbreviate the one-step scalar comparison by $d_K$. For $u\theta_K=\theta_LT_E(u)$, naturality gives $T_M(Su)d_K=d_LS(T_Eu)$. Consequently
$$Su\,(S\theta_K)d_K^{-1}=(S\theta_L)S(T_Eu)d_K^{-1}=(S\theta_L)d_L^{-1}T_M(Su).$$
Thus the transported structure is the stated $\theta_M$, its inverse is $d_KS(\theta_K^{-1})$, and every transported specified arrow is a Weil morphism. Only functoriality, the defining Weil equation and naturality of the cited comparison enter this calculation.

proof.text: At a fixed finite stage define $\theta_E^{[1]}=\theta_E$ and $\theta_E^{[r+1]}=\theta_E^{[r]}T_E^r(\theta_E)$. A functor sends an inverse to an inverse, since applying it to the two inverse identities gives the two inverse identities for the images. Hence induction makes every $\theta_E^{[r]}$ an isomorphism, with inverse $T_E^r(\theta_E^{-1})(\theta_E^{[r]})^{-1}$ at the successor step. The associative and unital composition comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identify each iterated pullback with $L(g_Y^r)_E^*$, and identify the recursion with the one in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

proof.text:
Prove the scalar equation by induction on $r\geq1$. The case $r=1$ is $\theta_Md_{1,K}=S\theta_E$. The coherent iterated comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] obey
$$d_{r+1,K}=T_M^r(d_{1,K})d_{r,T_EK},\qquad
T_M^r(S\theta_E)d_{r,T_EK}=d_{r,K}S(T_E^r\theta_E),$$
the second equation being naturality at $\theta_E:T_EK\to K$. Therefore the induction hypothesis gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_M^{[r+1]}d_{r+1,K}
&=\theta_M^{[r]}T_M^r(\theta_Md_{1,K})d_{r,T_EK}\\
&=\theta_M^{[r]}d_{r,K}S(T_E^r\theta_E)\\
&=S(\theta_E^{[r]})S(T_E^r\theta_E)=S(\theta_E^{[r+1]}).
\end{aligned}$$
All equations are in the rationalized constructible categories supplied by the cited comparison theorem; no new choice of integral representatives or reductions is made.

proof.text: For the identity extension the scalar comparison is the identity, so $\theta_E$ and every iterate are unchanged. For $E\subset M\subset N$, the tower compatibility in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] says that the direct comparison $d_{r,K}$ equals the composite through $M$ under the scalar associator. Substitute the scalar equation just proved, first for $E\subset M$ and then for $M\subset N$: the two adjacent comparisons cancel, leaving $\theta_N^{[r]}$ times that direct comparison equal to $\theta_E^{[r]}\otimes_E N$. This is also the direct-extension formula, so cancellation of the invertible direct comparison proves the tower equation for the iterates. For $r=1$ this proves that the Weil structures themselves agree under the associator.

proof.text: If two finite representatives give the same structure arrow, their underlying maps become equal over a common further field by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]; impose their inverse identities there as in steps 1--2. Inverses then agree: $v=v\theta w=w$ for any two inverses $v,w$ of $\theta$. Equal structure maps have equal iterates by the recursion. Step 5 shows that computing an iterate before enlarging the field gives the same class as computing it afterwards; step 6 compares direct and successive enlargement. Hence the classes $\theta^{[r]}:T^rK\to K$ are independent of representatives, chosen inverse representatives and the further fields used to witness equations. They are exactly the iterates formed by applying the common-stage functor $T$ to $\theta$ and composing, since that functor acts by the scalar-conjugated finite-stage maps in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

proof.text:
Finally work in the category $\mathcal C_Y$ with its functor $T$. For a Weil morphism $u:K\to L$ the case $r=1$ is its defining equation $u\theta_K=\theta_LT(u)$ in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. If $u\theta_K^{[r]}=\theta_L^{[r]}T^r(u)$, associativity and functoriality give
$$\begin{aligned}
u\theta_K^{[r+1]}
&=\theta_L^{[r]}T^r(u)T^r(\theta_K)
=\theta_L^{[r]}T^r(u\theta_K)\\
&=\theta_L^{[r]}T^r(\theta_LT(u))
=\theta_L^{[r+1]}T^{r+1}(u).
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the assertion for all positive $r$. No inverse of $u$ occurs. In particular, if finite models of the same Weil datum are related by an isomorphism, this equation also identifies their iterates through that isomorphism.
